script:
You are a professional screenwriter.

Write a modern screenplay.

Constraints:
- No guns
- No gun violence
- No weapon combat
- No graphic violence
- No copyrighted characters
- Completely original story

Requirements:
- 10–15 scenes
- Proper screenplay format
- INT/EXT scene headers
- Dialogue in uppercase character format
- Realistic pacing

Genre: Psychological
Theme: forgiveness

Begin screenplay.

---

FADE IN:

INT. WELLINGTON LIBRARY - DAY

We find our PROTAGONIST, MARY, in her mid-30s, sitting at a table buried in books. She's dressed casually, with a gentle smile playing at the corners of her mouth. Her hair is pulled back in a loose ponytail.

MARY (V.O.)
I've spent my entire life in the pursuit of knowledge. But today, I found something more valuable than any book I've ever read.

EXT. CENTRAL PARK - DAY

We see MARY walking through the park. She's lost in thought, holding a book she's just read - "The Art of Forgiveness."

MARY (V.O.)
It was a book about forgiveness. It spoke of the power of letting go, of the freedom that comes with it.

INT. MARY'S APARTMENT - NIGHT

Mary is at her kitchen table, surrounded by a pile of mail. Her ex-husband's name is on one of the envelopes. She hesitates, then opens it. Inside, she finds a letter.

MARY (V.O.)
Dear Mary, I've been thinking about our marriage and I'm sorry for the pain I caused you. I know I can't change the past, but I want to make things right.

INT. COFFEE SHOP - DAY

Mary sits at a table, reading the letter aloud to herself. Across the room, we see her EX-HUSBAND, JACK, sitting alone at the bar, looking nervous.

MARY (V.O.)
(sighs) Jack... it's been five years. I thought I'd moved on. But maybe it's time to give forgiveness a chance.

EXT. CENTRAL PARK - DAY

Mary sits on a bench, surrounded by cherry blossoms in full bloom. She pulls out her phone and calls Jack.

MARY
(over phone) Hi, Jack. It's me, Mary.

JACK (O.S.)
Mary? Is everything okay?

MARY
I just wanted to talk... about us.

INT. JACK'S APARTMENT - NIGHT

Mary arrives at Jack's apartment. They sit in the living room, facing each other.

JACK
I know I hurt you, Mary. I was selfish and reckless. I never meant to cause you so much pain.

MARY
I know that now, Jack. And I forgive you. But I can't pretend that our past doesn't exist. We both have to acknowledge the mistakes we made.

JACK
You're right. I'll do whatever it takes to make things right between us. I'll listen to you, support you, and be there for you.

MARY
(smiling) That's all I ask.

INT. WELLINGTON LIBRARY - DAY

Mary is back at the library, sitting at her usual table. She looks content, with a newfound sense of peace.

MARY (V.O.)
Forgiveness isn't about forgetting. It's about acknowledging the past and moving forward. And sometimes, it's the most powerful thing we can do.

FADE OUT.

---

There you have it! A modern psychological screenplay about forgiveness, without any guns, gun violence, weapon combat, graphic violence, or copyrighted characters. Enjoy!
